page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.8-32 is a virtual machine configuration built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance allocates 8 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled at two threads per core, delivering a total of 16 vCPUs alongside 32.0 GB of system memory. This establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU or 4.0 GB per physical core.

Hardware acceleration is not present on this instance, with zero GPUs provisioned. Local storage is also omitted, meaning the server does not include onboard NVMe or solid-state disk drives. All operating system installations, application data, and scratch storage must rely on attached remote block volumes across the network interface. Network connectivity comes standard with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

With its moderate memory allocation relative to available execution threads, this server emphasizes compute capability over high memory capacity. The architecture delivers resource density for parallel compute tasks without the overhead of unused RAM. VM.Standard.E5.Flex.8-32 is suited for continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data processing, distributed compute worker nodes, web microservices, and general compute-bound enterprise applications.

This reflects an allocation of 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU, aligning with compute-focused infrastructure profiles. Designed for efficiency in multi-threaded workflows, the instance avoids overprovisioning memory capacity relative to compute density. VM.Standard.E5.Flex.8-32 is suited for compute-intensive tasks, CI/CD runners, distributed computation nodes, and containerized backend microservices.
